about.title: About NEO SSH-Win Manager
about.desc:
A modern GUI frontend for sshfs-win.
Mount remote SSH filesystems as Windows drive letters.
about.what_it_does.title: Features
about.what_it_does.body: Mount remote SSH filesystems as Windows drive letters with one click. Multi-user support with encrypted credential storage. Built-in SSH terminal, system info panel, live tray toggles, and optional CLI companion for automation. Built on WinFsp + SSHFS-Win.

about.credits: Built on {winfsp} and {sshfs} – thanks to both projects.

telemetry.prompt.title: Help us improve NEO SSH-Win Manager
telemetry.prompt.body:
We would be delighted if you took part in our little "census".

What is sent?
An anonymous counter on installation, on login and when the update function is used (e.g. "+1 login"), together with the app version and the UI language.

What is not sent?
No personal or sensitive data at all – no usernames, no IP addresses, no data about your servers.

Why it helps:
We can see whether and how the project is used, which versions are in circulation and which translations matter. That motivates our small team to keep providing free updates.

You can change this decision at any time in the settings.
tip.title: Did you know?
tip.first_connection: Use the + above the list or Ctrl+N to add your first connection. Besides SFTP, the app also speaks FTP and FTPS.
tip.list_shortcuts: Ctrl+N adds a new connection, Ctrl+E edits the selected one. In the form, Ctrl+S saves and Esc cancels.
tip.filter: Long list? Ctrl+F filters it by name, host and user. Several words narrow it down further, and the filter stays in place after a restart.
tip.groups_intro: Sort your connections into groups, such as "web, client-a"; separate several groups with commas. Above the list you can then filter by group.
tip.groups_mount: When a group is selected above the list, "Mount All" and "Dismount All" only act on the connections in that group.
tip.groups_state: The group filter above the list also offers "Only mounted" and "Unmounted", so you see at a glance what is mounted right now.
tip.mount_all: The cloud above the list mounts all connections at once; the red × disconnects them all again.
tip.templates_intro: Often set up similar servers? Also save a connection as a template. New connections then start pre-filled, just without password and key.
tip.templates_use: When you add a connection, pick a template at the top. Everything is copied over, and the drive letter adjusts itself.
tip.context_menu: Right-click a connection to see every action. Under "SSH open with" you can use OpenSSH, PuTTY or the integrated terminal just this once.
tip.ask_auth: Password one day, key the next? With the method "Ask each time" you decide whenever you connect.
tip.status_folder: In a connection's details, a click on the grey folder mounts the drive. Once the folder is green, the same click opens it in Explorer.
tip.tray: Right-click the app icon in the system tray: there you connect and disconnect each connection with one click, without opening the window.
tip.close_to_tray: With "Minimize to system tray on close", the app keeps running when you close the window, and your drives stay connected.
tip.start_with_windows: Turn on "Start with Windows" in the settings. Together with "Auto-connect on start", your drives are there right after you sign in to Windows.
tip.auto_connect: "Auto-connect on start" in the settings mounts the drives that were connected last time again when the app starts.
tip.dir_cache: New files take a while to appear on the drive? "Disable directory cache" in the settings always loads folders fresh from the server, at the cost of a little more network traffic.
tip.shared_letters: Several hosts on the same drive letter? Allow it in the settings. Only one of them is mounted at a time, and if you like, the app falls back to a free letter.
tip.ghost_drives: A disconnected drive still lingers in Explorer? Turn on debug mode in the settings, and "Fix ghost drives" appears below it.
tip.windows_servers: Windows servers running OpenSSH work everywhere in the app: in the terminal, the file browser, system info and as a drive, even with a subfolder such as C:\Projects.
tip.quit_keep_mounted: When you log out, you can choose "Quit only": the app closes and your hosts stay mounted.
tip.terminal_tabs: The integrated terminal opens as many sessions per connection as you like, in tabs, with "Open another session".
tip.terminal_choice: Your terminal, your choice: in the settings, pick the integrated terminal, Windows OpenSSH or PuTTY for SSH.
tip.putty_ppk: PuTTY needs keys in .ppk format. Convert OpenSSH keys with PuTTYgen and enter the .ppk file in the connection form.
tip.file_browser: The folder marked "FTP" in the sidebar opens the file browser: all your hosts in tabs, no mounted drive needed.
tip.fb_split: In the file browser, F9 turns on split mode: this PC on the left, the server on the right. Drag files across, or send them to the other side with F6.
tip.fb_shortcuts: Press F1 in the file browser to see every keyboard shortcut at a glance.
tip.fb_undo: Moved or renamed something and regretted it right away? In the file browser, Ctrl+Z undoes it and Ctrl+Y redoes it. Deleted files don't come back this way, though.
tip.fb_bookmarks: Ctrl+D in the file browser bookmarks the current server folder, ideal for paths you need often.
tip.fb_url: Ctrl+Shift+L in the file browser puts a file from the web straight onto the server. If it can, the server downloads it itself.
tip.fb_archive: Uploading hundreds of small files? "Upload folder as archive" in the upload menu packs them first and unpacks them on the server, which is much faster.
tip.fb_sync: Ctrl+Shift+S in the file browser syncs folders between PC and server, with a preview before anything happens.
tip.fb_terminal: Ctrl+Shift+T in the file browser opens a terminal that is already in the current folder.
tip.fb_open_with: In the file browser, open files in the program of your choice (Ctrl+O). When you save them there, the app uploads them again by itself.
tip.fb_checksum: Want to be sure? In the file browser settings, the app can compare the SHA-256 checksum after every transfer.
tip.fb_resume: If the connection drops in the middle of a transfer, the file browser reconnects and continues where it stopped.
tip.fb_hidden: Where is the .htaccess? The file browser shows files that start with a dot once you turn them on in its settings.
tip.fb_speed: Transfers slowing everything else down? Set speed limits for uploads and downloads in the file browser settings.
tip.ftp_explorer: You can also open FTP connections in Windows Explorer: just right-click them.
tip.ftp_plain: Plain FTP sends even your password unencrypted. If the server supports FTPS, switch the connection's protocol to it.
tip.system_info: The "i" in a connection's details shows the server's CPU, RAM, drives and uptime live, on Linux and Windows alike.
tip.single_user_on: Only you use the app on this PC? In User Management you can enable single-user mode. The app then signs you in by itself, no password needed.
tip.single_user_account: Several people use this PC? Create an account with a password in User Management. Your connections and settings are kept.
tip.encryption: The app stores passwords, hosts and user names encrypted with AES-256, using a key that only your account can unlock.
tip.login_lockout: Guessing passwords is pointless: after several failed attempts the app locks the login for a while, longer each time.
tip.key_auth: Keys instead of passwords: with "Use private key" you sign in more securely. Set it under Method in the connection form.
tip.host_key: If the app reports that a known server's key has changed, check it carefully: it may be a reinstalled server, or an attack.
tip.login_language: On the login screen, pick the language at the top right. It becomes your language in the app right away.
tip.cli: For scripts and agents there is NeoSSHWinManager-cli.exe. Enable CLI access in a connection's form and use the access key shown there.
tip.cli_history: Everything run over the CLI is listed in the connection's details under "Show CLI history", with output and exit code.
tip.themes: Four themes are ready: Black, Blue (classic), Gray and Light. Switch them in the settings under Interface theme.
tip.accent: Make the app your own: in the settings, choose an accent color of your own, and the text color on it too, if you like.
tip.background_network: The network of dots in the background can be switched off in the settings, if you prefer it plain.
tip.languages: The app speaks English, German, Spanish, Russian, Dutch and Arabic, Arabic even from right to left.
tip.github: Found a bug or have an idea? On GitHub at gregorkrebs/neosshwinmanager every issue is welcome, bug reports and wishes alike.
tip.copy_version: For a bug report: under "About", "Copy version info" puts the app version and Windows build on the clipboard.
tip.help_buttons: The small question marks in the connection form open the online help right at the matching spot.
tip.demo: Colleagues curious? An interactive demo runs right in the browser at neosshwinmanager.org/app.
tip.telemetry: Help make the app better: the anonymous telemetry in the settings only sends counters, the version and the language. No names, no hosts, no IP addresses.
tip.updates: In the settings, "Check for updates" looks for a new version any time. If you like, an update installs itself the next time the app starts.
tip.fun_vim: Stuck in vim in the terminal? Esc, then :q! and Enter. You're welcome.
